headline: Deep learning classifies cardiac and neural states from ECG, EEG, and smartphone SCG
label: Deep Learning Physiological Signal Analysis
summary: Generalization across datasets and field-deployable sensing are now central demands, as shown by cross-dataset AF detection and smartphone SCG analysis.
synthesis: The shared thread is deep learning applied to noisy physiological waveforms for diagnostic classification or biomarker extraction. Methods are matched to the signal: time-frequency fusion with supervised contrastive learning for ECG atrial fibrillation detection, a CNN-GRU hybrid with MRMR feature selection for EEG depression classification, and attention-gated U-Net segmentation of smartphone seismocardiography to localize aortic valve opening. The AF study reports cross-dataset evaluation and the SCG work targets field conditions, both addressing generalization beyond curated data. ECGomics contributes a different emphasis, decomposing ECG into four biomarker dimensions that pair expert morphological rules with latent deep-learning features. What is new is the integration of learned representations with interpretable, deployment-oriented outputs rather than a single accuracy target; the reported EEG accuracy alone does not establish that advance.
